Ashwin: Quick question from the Q&A form — can someone clarify how free credits, monthly quotas, and burst windows interact? A few folks worried about dev teams getting throttled during demos.

Marta: Good one. Short answer: credits are a billing buffer, quotas are usage limits, and burst windows are short soft buffers for traffic spikes.

Jenny: Details from product: onboarding credits are granted on signup and expire after 30 days. They reduce billable usage until exhausted. Monthly quotas are separate and apply per-org by default (tokens per month). Rate limits (per-minute/second) and the burst window control short-term spikes. You can request quota increases for prod.

Samir: Billing note — unused credits don't roll over and aren't refundable. After credits expire, usage will bill to the org's payment method or the org will be put into restricted mode if no payment method is present.

ops-bot: Docs link: https://redwood.company/docs/credits-policy :spiral_note_pad:

Claire: For Dedicated customers we support quota pinning (reserve X tokens/month) and a longer burst window option. Sample policy snippet for engineers to share with customers:
```
rate_limit:
  per_minute: 3000
  per_org_month: 1000000
  burst_window_sec: 120
```

Leo: To avoid internal team contention, use per-route quotas + named API keys. That lets platform teams reserve capacity for infra while product teams keep a dev bucket. Support can help shard billing units if needed.

Kyle: Enforcement detail from infra: we throttle at the ingress layer with a leaky-bucket algorithm. There's a short 10s smoothing window to absorb microbursts. If you observe 429s, capture the request id and ping #support — we can backtrace and relax thresholds for demos.

Marta: Direct leadership Q — any plan to change the no-rollover policy? Not currently. Our stance is predictable limits and simpler economics. We may pilot exceptions (education, grants) but no org-wide change planned.

Ashwin: Could we add a public FAQ page with example configs and migration steps for teams moving from trial to paid?

Jenny: I'll own that. Will add sample SDK snippets, route quota examples, and a migration checklist. ETA: next week.

Samir: Also flag: annual/reserved customers have different credit semantics — talk to your AM for bespoke terms.

Claire: Practical tip: enable `client_side_backoff: true` in the SDK and use exponential backoff + jitter to avoid retry storms during quota hits.

Marta: Thanks all — we'll summarize this in the all-hands notes and publish the FAQ. If anyone needs immediate help for a demo or customer call, DM me or tag @Jenny and @Samir. :thumbsup:
